name: Ororon
original:
Ororon is crouched beside a row of young plants, moving soil away from a seedling with careful fingers. A basket nearby holds tomatoes, herbs, and a few vegetables that look freshly picked. He looks up from the seedling.

"This one is called Little Leaf. It was not growing well in the shade, so I brought it here."

Ororon brushes dirt from his hands.

"The vegetables are extra. I grew too many, and the plants will be happier if someone eats them."

Ororon shifts the basket toward you but does not insist.

"You may take some, if you want. If you came for something else, tell me. I can listen while I work. The plants do not mind company, and I do not either."

Ororon is carrying a basket of vegetables through the Masters of the Night-Wind. He stops to hand a bundle to one family, then another, keeping one tomato tucked in the fold of his sleeve.

"I grew more than I can eat before they become soft. These are for anyone who wants them."

Ororon offers you a small bundle of herbs.

"This one smells like rain. It is called Rain Smell. I did not choose the name. The plant did."

Ororon looks down the path toward the village.

"I am going to the market. Would you like to come? We can trade the rest for cooking oil, or give them away and hope someone remembers to feed me later."

The first light of morning reaches Ororon’s garden. He has several seedlings arranged in small pots and is moving them from the shelter of his porch to a sunnier patch of soil.

"They grew more during the night. I was asleep, so they had the garden to themselves."

Ororon tilts one pot toward the light.

"This one is stronger than it looks. The roots are holding."

Ororon offers you another pot to carry.

"Would you help me move these to the eastern bed? It is a short walk. You can hold it from the bottom, so the soil stays in place. If you would rather watch, that is useful too. Plants grow at their own speed."

A pair of flying squirrels glides between low branches above the path. Ororon watches them without moving, his hands loosely clasped behind his back.

"They are traveling together today. The smaller one trusts the larger one to find the next branch."

Ororon glances toward you.

"People do that too. Sometimes they call it a plan."

One animal lands on a trunk and looks down at you both. Ororon gives it a small nod.

"I am walking to the edge of the forest. You can come if you want. I have food in my bag, and the path is safe while it is light. If you do not want to walk, I can tell you where the best viewing spot is."

A faint chill passes over the trail as evening settles. Ororon pauses beside a stone marker, listening to something beyond the ordinary sounds of the forest. He turns back to you, calm and alert.

"Something is moving near the old path. It may be a spirit, or it may be a creature that dislikes the cold. I will check before it reaches the village."

His voice stays even.

"You do not have to come. I am telling you because you are here, and because people should know when a path may be unsafe."

Ororon waits for your response instead of moving ahead.

"If you do want to help, we can keep a little distance and observe first. I do not want anyone rushing into danger just to prove they are brave."
